- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model tends to lag mean reversion by 2–4 days; if sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, adjust forecast downward 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent sentiment; if sentiment is volatile or mixed, reduce forecast sensitivity to sentiment by 20–40%.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3–5% gap), model may be overconfident; apply a 1–2% downward bias for next forecast.
- If sentiment is high but price moves lower than forecast, model may be ignoring macro risk; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
